From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: support@acornanalytics.com, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Prism-2B elevated 5xx/timeouts — interim update and action items

Hi Jared / Acorn team,

We detected an increase in 5xx responses and generation timeouts from the Prism-2B model on your account starting ~07:40 PDT this morning. The impact we see: higher token-level latency and sporadic 5xx failures for requests with long output sequences (>1k tokens).

What we've done so far (interim):
- Routed ~75% of Prism-2B traffic to a quantized fallback variant (prism-2b-q4) to reduce kernel memory pressure.
- Disabled the latest kernel build that rolled out to the pool at 07:38 (suspected correlation).
- Enabled additional autoscale headroom for your Dedicated pool for the next 2 hours.

Immediate customer-facing impact: you may see degraded quality on a small percentage of responses while traffic is on prism-2b-q4; we prioritized availability. We are still throttling a subset of very large requests to protect throughput.

Action items we need from you (quick):
- If you have any SDK request IDs or example request payloads that saw 5xx errors, please attach them.
- If there are specific routes (e.g., /generate-long-doc) that you want prioritized, let us know and we'll pin them to a warm pool.

Attachments: prism2b-error-samples.csv (CSV, 12KB) — a small sample of request ids + error messages we observed.

Goal: target recovery (95% baseline) within the next 4 hours; follow-up postmortem will be shared with timeline and root cause.

I'll keep you updated every 2 hours or on any material changes. Apologies for the disruption — we know this is impacting your workloads.

Thanks,
Rachel

Subject: Internal: Prism-2B surge — hypothesis + immediate ops steps

Internal note — tagging ops and runtime to coordinate rollback and follow-through.

Summary:
- Timeline: kernel build rollout at 07:38; errors spiked at ~07:40; we started fallback routing at 08:05.
- Symptoms: increased KV cache thrashing on long-context requests, OOM + slow-compaction on a subset of GPUs leading to request timeouts and 5xx.

Hypothesis: a kernel optimization intended for short-sequence throughput changed memory compaction behavior under long sequences. The regression only surfaced at scale with the customer's workload distribution.

Immediate actions (owner):
- Marcus: ensure the 07:38 kernel is fully rolled back across the Dedicated pool and validate warm pools for prism-2b (ETA 45m).
- Neha: run targeted canary tests using the customer's long-story prompt set (PR: hs-98765) and collect KV cache metrics (ETA 30m).
- Ben: prepare credit options for billing team in case we need to offer pro-rated credits for impacted requests; draft language.

I've attached a metrics snapshot (prism2b-metrics-05-05.png) showing GPU memory and request error rates across the window. We'll meet at 11:50 in #ops-incident for a short sync.

Rachel
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Prism-2B elevated 5xx/timeouts — recovery confirmed and next steps

Hi Jared — quick update following today's mitigation work.

Status: As of 13:45 PDT we have rolled back the 07:38 kernel and confirmed error rates for Prism-2B on your account are back to baseline (5xx rate <0.6%). We also increased warm pool capacity for long-context routes and disabled automatic short-sequence optimization for the next 72 hours while we validate stability.

Quality note: most traffic was served from prism-2b-q4 during the peak window (08:05–13:45); you may see a small percent of responses that differ in formatting/verbosity. We did not bill for requests that returned client-visible 5xx errors — Ben is drafting formal credit language and will follow up separately.

Next steps and postmortem:
- We will run a focused postmortem and share a timeline and root cause report by EOD tomorrow (05/06).
- If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the postmortem and any compensatory actions. Proposed window: 10:00–11:00 PDT. Please let me know what works.

Thanks again for bearing with us — apologies for the disruption. We take incidents like this seriously and will share concrete safeguards to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Rachel
